c.tagline: The world's northernmost town — polar bears, glaciers, and the Arctic at the edge of the map.

taxi.fareNote: No ride-hailing apps operate this far north; Longyearbyen Taxi runs metered cars booked by phone, and in winter snowmobiles are the main way to reach anything beyond the short road network.

emergency.note: 112 police, 113 ambulance, 110 fire. Polar bears roam beyond the settlement — a rifle and flare gun are legally required when leaving town, but firearms must be left outside shops and public buildings.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Do not walk beyond the town's polar-bear warning signs without an armed, licensed guide — bears roam outside the settlement.
Crime is virtually nil — the real hazards are polar bears, avalanche terrain and extreme weather outside town limits.

hood_desc: The compact commercial heart along Vei 300 with the Svalbardbutikken department store, the town hall, restaurants, and most hotels; the natural, walkable base for first-time visitors.
'Old Longyearbyen' up the valley by the Longyear River, home to the historic Svalbard Church, early coal-mining relics, and a quiet character; best for travelers drawn to the town's mining heritage.
An elevated residential terrace above the centre near the school and the upscale Funken Lodge, with sweeping valley and fjord views; suits those wanting calm and a short walk down to town.
The 'new town' furthest up the valley in former miners' barracks, now budget guesthouses and student housing at the trailhead for glacier hikes; best for outdoorsy and budget travelers.
The largest residential neighborhood in the middle of the valley, quiet and local with easy access to the University Centre in Svalbard (UNIS); good for longer stays and a lived-in feel.

water.note: Tap water is glacial-fed and excellent.

transit.hours: There is no scheduled town bus service; the airport shuttle runs only to meet flights, and taxis operate on call.
transit.note: Longyearbyen has no public transport network. The compact centre is walkable; taxis, rental cars, and — in winter — snowmobiles cover longer distances, while organised tours handle any trip into the surrounding wilderness.
transit.pay: Taxis are paid by card or cash directly to the driver; there is no transit ticketing system.

ferry: Seasonal expedition cruises and boat tours (summer only)

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus (Flybussen) coordinated with flights, drops at hotels in town (~15 min)

tip.r: Service is included; rounding up or ~5-10% for good restaurant service is appreciated but never expected.
